what_it_is.prose: The T-90S Bhishma is the Indian Army's primary frontline main battle tank, based on the Russian T-90S platform and licence-produced at the Heavy Vehicles Factory (HVF) in Avadi, Tamil Nadu. India was the first export customer of the T-90, with the initial batch of 310 tanks imported from Russia in 2001–2003, followed by licensed production of additional units. The T-90S features a 125mm 2A46M smoothbore gun with an autoloader, capable of firing conventional ammunition and the 9M119 Refleks laser-guided anti-tank guided missile. It is powered by a V-92S2 V-12 diesel engine producing ~1,000 hp and protected by composite armour with Kontakt-1 explosive reactive armour (ERA) and the Shtora-1 infrared jamming system. The Indian T-90S is deployed across armoured corps formations on both the western (Pakistan) and northern (China) borders. India has pursued progressive upgrades to the T-90S fleet, incorporating improved thermal imaging, fire control, and ERA packages. The tank forms the bulk of India's armoured readiness alongside the older T-72 fleet and the indigenous Arjun Mk-1A.

deployments_procurement.summary: India initially imported 310 T-90S tanks from Russia (2001–2003) and subsequently ordered ~1,000+ additional units for licence production at HVF Avadi. The first Indian-built T-90S rolled out in 2007. The fleet is deployed across armoured corps formations on both borders.

faq.question: What is the difference between the T-72 and T-90S in Indian Army service?
faq.answer: The T-90S Bhishma is a more advanced evolution of the T-72 family, featuring improved composite armour with Kontakt-5 ERA (vs Kontakt-1 on upgraded T-72), a more powerful V-92S2 engine (~1,000 hp vs ~780 hp), the Shtora-1 IR jammer, and the 1A45T fire control system with improved thermal imaging. The T-90S also carries the 125mm 2A46M gun (an improved variant of the 2A46 on the T-72). The T-72 remains more numerous but the T-90S is the premium frontline MBT.

faq.question: How many T-90S tanks does India operate?
faq.answer: India operates an estimated 1,200–1,600 T-90S Bhishma tanks, making it one of the largest operators of the T-90 family globally. The exact fleet size is not publicly disclosed. The fleet comprises both imported Russian-built units (2001–2003) and Indian licence-produced units from HVF Avadi (2007 onwards).

faq.question: Does the T-90S fire missiles from its main gun?
faq.answer: Yes. The T-90S can fire the 9M119 Refleks (NATO: AT-11 Sniper) laser-guided anti-tank guided missile from its 125mm smoothbore gun. This gives the tank the ability to engage enemy armoured targets beyond the effective range of conventional tank gun ammunition, with a maximum range of approximately 4–5 km.
